Local-runs: probe — on a detached worktree of the head: `node scripts/pm/fleet-write/validate.mjs --self-test` (268 cases, 15 batteries, exit 0), `execute.mjs --self-test` (232 cases, 21 batteries, exit 0), `dispatch.mjs --self-test` (277 cases, 25 batteries, exit 0), `node scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs` (exit 0, total ceilings down 496) and `--self-test` (164 cases, exit 0), `check-skill-id-lint.mjs` (107 files clean, exit 0); then eight reviewer-authored ablations, each applied to the worktree, measured and restored with `git checkout` to a clean tree at the head sha (results in ①.11); the worktree was removed after the runs and the main working tree was not touched
Scope: .github/workflows/fleet-write.yml, scripts/pm/fleet-write/ops.mjs, scripts/pm/fleet-write/validate.mjs, scripts/pm/fleet-write/execute.mjs, scripts/pm/fleet-write/dispatch.mjs, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/rest-channel.md, scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs (the gate that enforces the rest-channel row, its header and its CROSS_FILE_MOVES map) + the code the hunks assert on, read not reviewed: scripts/pm/write-pace.mjs (`noteResponse`, `stopSignalFrom`, `markerText`, what they do with a response body), scripts/pm/fleet-token.mjs (`scrub`), scripts/pm/label-write.mjs (`classifyHttp`), AGENTS.md directive 14 (the Tier H landing rule), card #29160 body (Change §1–6, Out of scope, Acceptance, read as the contract), the seat's claim 6573114495 and raise comment 6572738609, the dev report 6574033806 (read as input)

Reviewer: an isolated contract reviewer at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER, read-only on GitHub, fed the card #29160 body, the seat's claim 6573114495, the dev's os-dev-report 6574033806 (read as input, not as conclusions), the PR body, the net diff against origin/main (merge-base 14208f2c; main has since moved to 49aba82b and none of the seven touched files moved with it), the head's check-runs, contract-review.md and review-checklist.md. The card, the PR and this record carry no finding, no mechanism, no advisory id and no title; the only ids anywhere in the diff are self-test fixtures that name no real advisory, and none is repeated here.

### ① Derived judgments

Accepted-set and public-surface changes, one by one, against the card's Change §1–6, Out of scope and Acceptance:

1. Change §1, the payload leaves the logged environment (fleet-write.yml, validate.mjs, execute.mjs). Both `FLEET_WRITE_PAYLOAD: ${{ toJSON(github.event.client_payload) }}` lines are gone; the validate step runs `validate.mjs --from-event --github-output` and the execute step's `env:` carries `FLEET_WRITE_SENDER` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` only. `readEventPayload` (validate.mjs, shared with execute.mjs) reads `$GITHUB_EVENT_PATH`, returns `event.client_payload`, and every refusal sentence names the variable and the failure class only (absent path, unreadable with the error code, not JSON, no client_payload object), never the file's text; the self-test pins it with a marker in the file. `--from-env` is removed from `KNOWN_FLAGS` and pinned gone; the executor's old route is pinned to read nothing. This covers every op, not only the new ones (card §1 second bullet). Correct.
   - Workflow grep at head: the only non-comment line naming `client_payload` is the pre-existing `run-name: 'fleet-write ${{ github.event.client_payload.request_id }}'` (the request id, 64 characters max, generated by dispatch.mjs); no `toJSON(github.event…)`, no `github.event.client_payload` in a `run:` or an `if:`, no `set -x`, no `shell:` override; the two `run:` lines are pinned verbatim by the self-test. `permissions: {}` at the top and `contents: read` on the job are unchanged. The mint step gains exactly one input, `permission-repository-advisories: ${{ steps.validate.outputs.permission_repository_advisories }}`, read from the validator's output and never a literal (pinned: one such line, no literal `read|write` spelling, one mint step, so no second un-narrowed token to fall back to), with the comment recording the measured run and that the action's "Unexpected input(s)" warning is expected and must not be removed (pinned by `workflowText.includes(...)`). `githubOutputLines` spells the hyphen as `_`, matching the workflow's `outputs.permission_repository_advisories` (pinned by the `--from-event --github-output` case). Correct; no new secret exposure.
2. Change §2, the three rows (ops.mjs). `advisory_report` (required `summary`, `description`; optional `severity`, `cwe_ids`; one `POST .../security-advisories/reports`, body exactly those keys), `advisory_collaborators_add` (`ghsa_id`, `collaborators` capped at `MAX_LOGINS_PER_ACTION` like `assignees`, `LOGIN_SHAPE` per item), `advisory_state` (`ghsa_id`, `advisory_state`); each `alone: true`, each `permission: 'repository-advisories'`, which is added to `PERMISSIONS` and to `STROKE_SCOPED_PERMISSIONS`. The `ghsa` field kind is its own closed kind (`GHSA_ID_SHAPE`, GHSA plus three groups of four lowercase alphanumerics), and its refusal names the shape and the value's length, never the value. `advisory_state` is an enum of exactly `ADVISORY_SETTABLE_STATES = ['draft','closed']` with `published` in `named` so it is refused by name with its reason; the self-test pins that no enum of any field admits `published` and that no request any row spells, at every enum value of every field, carries `publish` in a path, body or GraphQL. The two PATCH bodies are the executor's, not the table's (`'body' in req` is false, pinned). `REFUSED_PATH_FAMILIES` gains a negative-lookahead family that refuses every `security-advisories` path but one advisory's own path and the reports endpoint; the self-test covers the list, the draft create, the CVE request, the fork, trailing text and malformed ids. Correct and inside Out of scope (no publish, no draft create, no text read or edit, no collaborator removal).
3. Change §3, the validator. Field kinds, the `quiet` and `named` modifiers, the `shape`/`itemWhat` list modifier, fixtures and two new batteries (event file 6, advisory rows 44), floor 13 → 15, equal to two batteries added. A `str` refusal was already echo-free (type, emptiness or byte count only), so `summary` and `description` refusals never carry text (pinned with a prose marker in an over-cap description and in a non-string summary); `severity`, `cwe_ids`, `collaborators`, `advisory_state` are `quiet` and describe a failing value by type and size; unknown keys (`vulnerabilities`, `state`, `credits`, `body`, `cvss_vector_string`, `start_private_fork`, `collaborating_users`…) are refused by name without the value. Correct.
4. Change §4, the executor, in the shape of the `subIssue` path. `advisoryPreflight` GETs the advisory, judges `ADVISORY_FENCES` (read answers 200 with an advisory; the id is the one named; state in `ADVISORY_OPEN_STATES` for collaborators, in `ADVISORY_TRANSITIONS[to]` for a move), and a failing fence returns `not sent`, zero writes, exit 5. `advisoryCollaboratorPlan` lowercases both sides, adds each missing login once, and `merged` is the existing logins as the platform lists them followed by the missing ones; `missing` empty is a `not sent` no-op row, exit 0 (pinned: an all-present list sends no PATCH; a differently-cased existing login is not re-added; existing logins survive as the first elements of the sent body). `advisoryReadBack` lands only when the PATCH answer lists every missing login and every existing login (stricter than the card's "every requested login", correctly so); `advisoryStateReadBack` lands only on the named id in the requested state; `advisoryReportReadBack` lands only on a 2xx carrying a shaped `ghsa_id`, and a 2xx without one is a failed action saying UNCONFIRMED, do not re-send, no annotation. Transitions pinned: draft only from triage; closed only from triage or draft; seven illegal moves each `not sent`. The report's id goes into the row (`advisoryReportLandedText`) and into one notice annotation (`relayAdvisoryAnnotationMessage`, id only, parsed back by the reader's own parser). Battery floor 20 → 21, one battery added. Correct.
5. Change §4's ⛔ (rows, logs, step summary, annotations carry id, state and logins only). Every advisory row string is built by `advisoryPrintable`, which prints a value only when it matches `GHSA_ID_SHAPE`, `ADVISORY_STATE_SHAPE` or `LOGIN_SHAPE` and otherwise a placeholder; a platform `message` is quoted only when it is one of six fixed strings in `ADVISORY_PLATFORM_MESSAGES`; `resultOf` (which prints `html_url`) is never reached by an advisory row; `summaryText` prints `request_id`, `session`, `repo`, the action count and the rows' `call`/`status`/`result` only; `rest()` derives `detail` from `json.message` alone and the pace log (`noteResponse`) pattern-matches the body and never echoes it; the validator's success line prints request id, repo, session and op names. Traced leak paths, all closed: the step `env:` (removed and pinned), `run:`/`if:` expressions (none), the validator's refusals (type and size only), the executor's log lines, rows, summary and annotations (shape-gated), JSON dumps of payload or response (none in execute.mjs; dispatch.mjs `--json` emits request_id, state, read_back, annotations, advisories, runs, no payload), the executor's `--payload-file` parse error (now constant text, not the parser's message), and the dispatch read-back (none for advisory rows; `readBackTargets` is empty for a report stroke). Correct.
6. Change §5, dispatch.mjs. The report is in `CONTENT_CREATING_OPS` (rule ⑤ pacing) via `PROSE_KEYS` gaining `summary` and `description`, but not in `BODY_OPS`, so no read-back locator exists; the comment above `READ_BACK_LOCATORS` says why, and a self-test pins that the sentence sits above that declaration. `ADVISORY_ANNOTATED_OPS`, `relayAdvisoryAnnotationMessage`, `parseRelayAdvisoryAnnotation` (anchored regex, lowercase id only) and `matchRunAdvisories` (one id per action, else ignored) hand the id on as `result.annotations.advisories` and `--json` `advisories`; a report no annotation names stays exit 0 with one line saying where the id is and never to re-send. Seat battery 12 cases, floor 24 → 25. The seat-side lines name the id only (pinned with a marker). Correct.
7. Change §6, rest-channel.md: exactly one line added (80 → 81 lines, measured on the committed blobs), 116 bytes, naming the three ops and that publishing is the maintainer's. Correct.
8. The sender gate: no hunk in execute.mjs touches the permission read or `gate.role`; the ruling 「所有车队账户都能发这个操作」 is recorded beside the rows in ops.mjs (the OPS comment and the header section) with what it admits. Correct.
9. The ratchet row: 80 → 81 equals the measured delta of +1; the comment quotes the maintainer verbatim from the card body (filing-gate ③, the same ruling-of-record convention cr11 accepted for #29111) and the seat's raise comment 6572738609, which stated 80 → 81 at most by the measured delta. No other row or map entry changed. rest-channel.md is a SOURCE of the platform-readings cross-file move (`was` 93); raising a source's ceiling reduces that move's net source decrease by one, and the gate still reads the move as paid down (all 144 lines the destination stands above its `was` are recorded `ruledRaises`), so condition (a) holds. The self-test is unchanged and green. Correct.
10. Acceptance, item by item: the three self-tests pass with the new batteries counted (my runs: 268/15, 232/21, 277/25, equal to the dev's); malformed `ghsa_id` refused before any request (validator, 14 shapes; executor gate case with zero requests); a stroke with another action beside one of these rows refused (validator, packer); only these strokes' tokens carry the grant (every other op alone and the all-share-one-token stroke write an EMPTY `permission_repository_advisories` and mint no such grant; the two actions strokes mint no advisory grant); existing collaborators survive; all-present sends no PATCH; each illegal transition sends no PATCH; `published` refused by name; an answer not showing the result fails the action for all three rows; no `env:` carries `client_payload` with a positive control that finds a planted block env and an inline env; the marker test over 32 executor runs plus four real `validate.mjs`/`execute.mjs` processes reading an event file that carries the marker, with positive controls (every served answer carried it; the generic printer would print it). All present. The last box (the live run) is post-merge by the card's own words and is listed in the PR body's Acceptance notes, item for item as the card lists it.
11. Ablations, mine, each restored to a clean tree at the head sha: A the landed report row also prints the answer's summary → execute 2 of 232 red (row shape and the marker test); B any platform message quoted on a refusal → execute 3 of 232 and validate 1 of 268 red; C a quiet enum echoes its value → validate 1 of 268 and dispatch 1 of 277 red; D the validate step's `env:` carries `client_payload` again → validate 2 of 268 red (the empty-list pin and the one-live-line pin); E the state fence sentence carries the answer's summary → execute 1 of 232 (marker test) and validate 2 of 268 red; F `severity` loses `quiet` → validate 2 of 268 and dispatch 1 of 277 red; G the executor logs the request body before the write → execute 1 of 232 red (marker test); H advisory rows fall through to the generic landing and row printer → execute 8 of 232 red, the marker reaching the rows through `html_url`. The dev's four ablations (A–D) reproduce with the same counts. The guards are load-bearing and the batteries fail when they are removed.
12. Surface: exactly the seven claimed files, nothing else; no `content/docs/releases/`, no published package, `skip-changeset` is right (scripts/pm, a workflow and a skill reference publish nothing). PR is draft, targets main, head repo is the base repo, author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`. The PR body matches the head: battery counts and floors, the `REFUSED_PATH_FAMILIES` description, `ADVISORY_PLATFORM_MESSAGES`, the UNCONFIRMED sentence, `--json` `advisories`, the ratchet 80 → 81, the ablation blobs (execute 556168a3, validate 134579ec, workflow 8e31d25d all equal the head's blob ids). Its Acceptance notes list what only the post-merge live run decides, in the card's four items plus the refusal rule (never a wider token).
   - Should-fix (S1): the body says `Fixes #29160` while the card's last Acceptance box ("After merge, one live run … report the run links and the results") is decided only after merge; review-checklist says `Fixes` only when the merge should close the card, otherwise `Part of`. Either spell it `Part of #29160` so the card stays open to receive the live run's reading (a refused action there goes to the maintainer and needs a carrier), or the seat states in its ACCEPT where the live run is tracked. A body edit, no new head.
   - Should-fix (S2): two comments lag the three-row design: ops.mjs's `alone` descriptor comment says "`advisory_collaborators_add`'s, the one spending `repository-advisories: write`" and validate.mjs's `tokenPermissionsOf` doc says "an `advisory_collaborators_add` one, which adds `repository-advisories: write`", while all three rows spend it (the header, `PERMISSIONS` doc and the self-tests say three). Comments only; behaviour is right.
   - Should-fix (S3): the ratchet row's new comment has two lines of 132 and 136 bytes where the block wraps at about 120; no gate caps it (ESLint green). Re-wrap.
   - Observation, no fix: dispatch.mjs `--dry-run` prints the whole `client_payload`, a report's `summary` and `description` included, to the seat's stdout by design; it is seat-local, not a relay surface, and the seat's own record discipline (card #29111's rule) keeps it off any public surface. The `run-name` renders the request id before validation; the id is generated by dispatch.mjs and the self-test pins it as the one live line naming `client_payload`.

### ② Semver level

None. No published package, no `packages/spec/src/**`, no TypeScript; relay scripts under scripts/pm, one workflow, one skill reference line and one ratchet data row. `skip-changeset` is the right declaration and the Check Changeset check is green. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are correct.

- Dev `open_questions`: empty; `out_of_scope_findings`: empty. Nothing to answer or escalate.
- Dev deviation: the seat brief asked for a ready PR, the relay forces draft on `pr_create`, so the PR is a draft; on this Tier H diff readying it is the seat's hand-off and the `pr_ready` follow-up requests `GOVERNED_APPROVERS`. Consistent with AGENTS.md directive 14 (Tier H lands only by an authorized approval and the maintainer's hand). No flag.

All four are listed in the PR body and in ops.mjs's header, with the rule that a refusal goes to the maintainer and is never retried under a wider token (`ADVISORY_ACCESS_REMEDY`, pinned on every refusal path).

### ④ Design judgment

For each hits file, against the card's scenario (a seat files a private report through the relay, adds who works it, accepts and closes, reads under its own account, and no advisory text reaches a public surface) and the code it cites:

- `.github/workflows/fleet-write.yml`: the design holds. The payload's only route to the scripts is the runner-written event file; the one stroke-scoped mint input is read from the validator's output exactly like `permission-actions`; the warning note is beside the input; `permissions` unchanged; the self-test reads the workflow text and pins both the absence (block and inline `env:`) and the presence (one mint line, one mint step, the warning text, the two `run:` lines).

Holds; ablations A, B, E, G, H confirm the guards are load-bearing.
- `scripts/pm/fleet-write/dispatch.mjs`: the read-back exception is said where the read-back is decided and pinned; the id travels back by annotation only; the floor rose by one battery. Holds.
